result.topic_en: Derivation of the differential variations of orbital inclination i and node longitude Ω of a planet perturbed by another body (perturbing forces X, Y, Z), starting from the fundamental equations of motion in rectangular and polar coordinates.
result.transcription:
Es seyn die Fundamentalgleichungen
$0 = \frac{\partial\partial x}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\Theta x}{r^3} + X$ \quad $X = \mu\left(\frac{x-x'}{\varrho^3} + \frac{x'}{r'^3}\right)$
$0 = \frac{\partial\partial y}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\Theta y}{r^3} + Y$ \quad $Y = \mu\left(\frac{y-y'}{\varrho^3} + \frac{y'}{r'^3}\right)$
$0 = \frac{\partial\partial z}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\Theta z}{r^3} + Z$ \quad $Z = \mu\left(\frac{z-z'}{\varrho^3} + \frac{z'}{r'^3}\right)$
$s = r\cos b,\ \theta = \tang \beta$
$0 = \frac{\partial\partial s - s\partial\lambda^2}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\Theta s}{r^3} + X\cos\lambda + Y\sin\lambda$
$0 = \frac{s\partial\partial\lambda + 2\partial s\partial\lambda}{\partial t^2} - X\sin\lambda + Y\cos\lambda$
$0 = \frac{s\partial\partial\theta + 2\partial s\partial\theta + s\theta\partial\lambda^2}{\partial t^2} - X\theta\cos\lambda - Y\theta\sin\lambda + Z$
$\mathrm{tg}\, i\cos\Omega = P = \theta\sin\lambda + \frac{\partial\theta}{\partial\lambda}\cos\lambda$
$\mathrm{tg}\, i\sin\Omega = Q = -\theta\cos\lambda + \frac{\partial\theta}{\partial\lambda}\sin\lambda$
$\partial P = \frac{\partial\partial\theta.\cos\lambda}{\partial\lambda} - \frac{\partial\partial\lambda.\partial\theta.\cos\lambda}{\partial\lambda^2} + \theta\cos\lambda\partial\lambda$
$\frac{s\,dP\,\partial\lambda^2}{\cos\lambda\,\partial t^2} = X\{\theta\cos\lambda\partial\lambda - \sin\lambda\partial\theta\} + Y\{\theta\sin\lambda\partial\lambda + \cos\lambda\partial\theta\} - Z\partial\lambda = R$
$\partial Q = \frac{\partial\partial\theta.\sin\lambda}{\partial\lambda} - \frac{\partial\partial\lambda.\partial\theta.\sin\lambda}{\partial\lambda^2} + \theta\sin\lambda\partial\lambda$
$+\frac{s\,dQ\,d\lambda^2}{\sin\lambda\,\partial t^2} = X\{\theta\cos\lambda\partial\lambda - \sin\lambda\partial\theta\} + Y\{\theta\sin\lambda\partial\lambda + \cos\lambda\partial\theta\} - Z\partial\lambda = R$
Hieraus
$\partial i = \frac{\cos i.\partial t^2}{s\partial\lambda}\left\{-X\sin i\sin\Omega + Y\sin i\cos\Omega - Z\cos i\right\}\cos(\lambda-\Omega)$
$\partial\Omega = \frac{\partial t^2}{\sin i.s.\partial\lambda}\left\{-X\sin i\sin\Omega + Y\sin i\cos\Omega - Z\cos i\right\}\sin(\lambda-\Omega)$
(Was in Parenthese steht wird
$\mu s'\left\{\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right\}.\left\{\sin i\sin(\lambda'-\Omega) - \cos i.\tang b'\right\}$
$\partial i = \frac{\mu r s'.\partial t.\cos(v-\Omega)}{k\sqrt{p}}\left\{\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right\}.\left\{\sin i\sin(\lambda'-\Omega) - \cos i.\mathrm{tg}\, b'\right\}$
$\partial\Omega = \frac{\mu r s'.\partial t.\sin(v-\Omega)}{\sin i.k\sqrt{p}}\left\{\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right\}.\left\{\sin i\sin(\lambda'-\Omega) - \cos i\,\mathrm{tg}\, b'\right\}$
$\partial i = \frac{\mu r r' k\partial t.\cos(v-\Omega)}{\Theta\sqrt{p}}\left(\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right).\left(\sin(v'-\Omega').(\sin i\cos i'\cos(\Omega'-\Omega) - \cos i\sin i') + \cos(v'-\Omega').\sin i\sin(\Omega'-\Omega)\right)$
$\partial\Omega = \frac{\mu r r' k dt\,\sin(v-\Omega)}{\sin i.\Theta\sqrt{p}}\left(\frac{1}{r'^3} - \frac{1}{\varrho^3}\right).\left(\sin(v'-\Omega')(\sin i\cos i'\cos(\Omega'-\Omega) - \cos i\sin i') + \cos(v'-\Omega')\sin i\sin(\Omega'-\Omega)\right)$

methods.what: Equations of motion of a perturbed planet in rectangular coordinates with perturbing forces from a third body
Transformation of equations of motion to cylindrical coordinates (s, λ, θ = tan of latitude)
methods.quote: $0 = \frac{\partial\partial s - s\partial\lambda^2}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\Theta s}{r^3} + X\cos\lambda + Y\sin\lambda$

methods.what: Expression of inclination and node through P = tan i cos Ω, Q = tan i sin Ω in terms of θ and dθ/dλ
Differential equations for variation of P and Q under perturbing forces
Variation of inclination in terms of the force component normal to the orbit plane
methods.quote: $\partial i = \frac{\cos i.\partial t^2}{s\partial\lambda}\left\{-X\sin i\sin\Omega + Y\sin i\cos\Omega - Z\cos i\right\}\cos(\lambda-\Omega)$

methods.what: Variation of node longitude in terms of the normal force component
methods.quote: $\partial\Omega = \frac{\partial t^2}{\sin i.s.\partial\lambda}\left\{-X\sin i\sin\Omega + Y\sin i\cos\Omega - Z\cos i\right\}\sin(\lambda-\Omega)$

methods.what: Normal force component expressed via the perturbing body's position
Final formulas for di and dΩ in terms of orbital elements of both bodies (true anomalies, inclinations, nodes)
